content.text:
Only MgScAlO4 (mp-1221961) is present.

I simulated MgScAlO4 and EuY2O4 and compared them with the observed pattern by eye:

- **MgScAlO4 matches.** Its simulated peaks fall at the same positions as the observed ones, with similar relative heights: about 10.6, 21.25, 29.6 (strongest), 30.5, 31.3, 34.3, 37.4, 44.4, 48.2, 57.3, 65.7, 67.1, 71.1, 75.5 and 78.4°. The weak shoulder near 70.4° and the small peak near 75.5° are also in its simulation.
- **EuY2O4 does not match.** It has no peaks at 10.6° or 21.25°. Those are the 8.3 Å and 4.2 Å layer spacings seen in the observed pattern.
- **Second phase:** I found no clear observed peak that MgScAlO4 fails to account for, so I see no evidence for one. I did not simulate the other seven candidates, so that rests on this residual check alone.

{"present": ["mp-1221961"], "confidence": 0.93, "note": "The MgScAlO4 simulation reproduces all observed peak positions and relative heights (10.6, 21.3, 29.6, 34.3, 57.3, 65.7, 71.1, 78.4 deg), with no clear unexplained peaks left over."}
